craft_notes: Sthāyin: śṛṅgāra of bounded hunger; vyabhicāri love sharpened to exact fullness. Sanskrit-first: grahaṇa (GRASP — kept grasping; hunger of seizure, not curiosity); ūna-adhika-nishedha (NEITHER-less-NOR-more — two bounds kept). Rows: 11 (‘His alone’ — belonging pointed exactly where Sanskrit points), 9 (never-little/never-more pair), 1 (‘never more’ closes — exactness sealed). Close: ‘never little, never more’. Rupture: semicolon (whose turns to how-much). Rejected: ‘hungry to know’ — killed: grasp kept; ‘fills everything perfectly’ — killed: ‘in all beings’ located + two bounds kept; ‘the supreme goddess Hers’ — killed: awkward possession, ‘His alone is’ kept. Read aloud: HIS a-LONE IS the GOD-dess su-PREME, HUN-gry TO-grasp HIS-na-ture … FULL-ness IN-all-BE-ings — NEV-er LITT-le, NEV-er MORE.

lines: His alone is the goddess supreme, hungry to grasp His nature;
fullness in all beings — never little, never more.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tasyaivaiṣā parā devī svarūpāmarśanotsukā | pūrṇatvaṃ sarvabhaveṣu yasyā nālpaṃ na cādhikam

reads_against.argmap: Whose is the goddess, and what does she want? → Belonging, bounded eagerness, exact fullness.
c1_essence: His goddess, grasp-eager, fills all exactly — never short, never over.
